CB1.title: derive a verdict's principal from its signature instead of its claim
CB1.commit: feat(verdict): derive the principal from an ssh signature
CB1.note:
ADR-0080 records that events.py checks only that the declared actor equals the declared principal and the channel says cli, so **a local agent process can write a syntactically valid declared-principal verdict**. This closes that.

Use `ssh-keygen -Y sign` and `-Y verify`, with the principal read from `-Y find-principals` and NEVER from a caller-supplied field. The project must hold no private key and no secret of any kind. A verdict must be verifiable years later by a third party from a clone alone -- if it is only verifiable by us, we could have fabricated it, which defeats the purpose.

AN.title: make A2 decidable while the log is being written
AN.commit: fix(doctor): decide A2 against a pinned prefix, not the live tail
AN.note:
MEASURED 24 Aug 2026. A2 is not failing because replay is broken -- replay reproduces exactly. It fails because `doctor` compares the persisted projection against a replay of the *live* log, and with ~20 agents appending, events land between the two reads. Observed in one sitting, same repository, minutes apart: FAIL ('canonical state diverged'), then UNKNOWN ('state covers N of M events'), then PASS -- the last only because the rebuild and the check happened in the same instant.

So the condition as written is decidable only on a quiet repository, and this repository is never quiet. A gate that reports three different verdicts for one unchanged history is measuring contention, not replay.

Fix it by deciding A2 against a **pinned prefix**: take the projection's own high-water mark, replay exactly that many events, and compare. Events appended after the mark are outside the comparison -- they are not evidence of divergence and must not be reported as such. A genuine mismatch inside the prefix must still FAIL, and an empty prefix must still be UNKNOWN (do not reintroduce the tautological pass repaired on 20 Aug 2026).

The test is the point of this unit: `tests/test_doctor_a2_concurrent.py` must append to the log *while* the check runs and assert the verdict is stable and correct. A test that only runs on a quiet log reproduces the bug it is meant to catch.

Do NOT make A2 pass by widening what counts as identical. The divergence report is right in principle; the read window is what is wrong.

AO.title: record the 22 August capture loss as baseline, once torn appends are refused
AO.commit: docs(adr): baseline the 22 August capture loss, contingent on AB
AO.note:
DECIDED by Joe, 24 Aug 2026. MEASURED same day: A3 is permanently unpassable as written. `pass` requires `run >= 7 AND new_refused == 0`. `run_start` walks backwards through consecutive capture days; 19-24 August are consecutive with no gap; three lines on 2026-08-22 (offsets 27, 35, 45) are invalid JSON, written by something that bypassed `append()`. Because the run never slides forward while capture continues daily, those three stay inside the window forever. The only way the current code passes is to STOP CAPTURING for a day, which resets run_start past the 22nd -- a capture gate you pass by breaking capture.

Write ADR-0105 recording those three digests as a known, permanent loss, exactly as ADR-0043 did for the original three, and add them to HISTORICAL_REFUSAL_DIGESTS. A3 then measures NEW loss going forward, which is what it is for.

**This unit must not land before AB.** AB makes a torn append refuse and name its offset. Baselining a loss whose cause is still live turns A3 into a ratchet that absorbs every future corruption and detects nothing -- that is the objection Joe was shown and the reason for the dependency. State it plainly in the ADR's 'evidence against' section, along with the rule: the baseline may only ever absorb a loss whose cause has been fixed and whose fix has shipped.

Do NOT widen A3, change its arithmetic, or make it a trailing window. The condition is right; the history under it is damaged.

AQ.title: release the claims of a dispatch that never started
AQ.commit: fix(coordination): release claims held by a run that never started
AQ.note:
MEASURED 24 Aug 2026. N00 gave us detection: the driver reports START_FAILED when a run writes no artefact inside the start window. Nothing releases what that run claimed, so its paths stay locked for the full hour. Observed in one tick: two dispatches died at startup (0 bytes after 509s and 432s) and their claims then refused T01 and AA -- T01 being the unit that gates 22 others. The hour was spent twice over on runs that were never alive.

`close_claim(log, run_id=...)` already exists and is properly attributed to DISPATCH_ACTOR; `live_claims` already treats a terminal dispatch event as a release. The missing half is calling it.

**The hazard is the whole of this unit.** Releasing the claim of a run that is merely SLOW, rather than dead, admits two agents to one path -- exactly what the claim exists to prevent, and a far worse outcome than an hour's delay. So a release must be justified by evidence the process is gone, not by absence of an artefact. Establish liveness properly: map the run to its process and confirm it is not running, and refuse to release when liveness cannot be determined. Fail closed.

Do NOT shorten the claim expiry to paper over this, and do NOT release on artefact silence alone. A silent process holding a lock and a dead one look identical from the artefact; that is the whole difficulty and the reason this is its own unit.
